question:
A 53-year-old male comes to the emergency department after discovering his blood pressure was
185/100 mmHg during a home measurement. He discontinued his prescribed lisinopril and
hydrochlorothiazide one month ago, believing they were causing fatigue. He reports a mild headache
(3/10 intensity). His vital signs show: - Temperature: 97.5°F (36.4°C) - Blood pressure: 182/92 mmHg -
Pulse: 87/min - Respiratory rate: 15/min - Oxygen saturation: 98% on room air Physical examination
reveals: - Normal cardiac sounds (S1, S2) - Clear lung sounds - 20/20 vision bilaterally - Normal
fundoscopic exam - Intact cranial nerves II-XII - Stable gait - ECG unchanged from baseline What is
the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Immediate IV labetalol (B)
Captopril and neurological monitoring (C) Amlodipine and transfer to ICU (D) Esmolol (E) Ibuprofen
and resume the patient's home blood pressure medications (F) Nitroprusside (G) Esmolol and
nicardipine (H) Clonidine and observation for 6 hours (I) Furosemide and strict bed rest (J) Hydralazine
and admission to telemetry
 A. Ibuprofen and resume the patient's home blood pressure medications
B. Amlodipine and transfer to ICU
C. Esmolol and nicardipine
D. Clonidine and observation for 6 hours
E. Captopril and neurological monitoring
F. Nitroprusside
G. Furosemide and strict bed rest
H. Hydralazine and admission to telemetry
I. Esmolol

J. Immediate IV labetalol
